candidate.blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.31 > Crisis Intervention: assess potential for violence and use safety precautions; identify the client in crisis; use crisis-intervention techniques to assist coping; guide the client to resources for recovery from crisis. Psychosocial Integrity activity statements also include therapeutic communication and assessment of support systems.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — crisis intervention, safety, therapeutic communication, and resource connection
candidate.educational_objective: Prioritize immediate safety assessment, supportive therapeutic listening, identification of urgent needs, and connection to appropriate resources during early crisis intervention before comprehensive history-taking or long-term treatment planning.

options.A: Complete a comprehensive lifetime psychiatric history before asking about immediate safety concerns.
options.B: Assess immediate safety and urgent needs, use calm supportive listening to understand the crisis, and connect the client with appropriate crisis resources.
options.C: Begin long-term psychotherapy goals before identifying the immediate problem that precipitated the crisis.
options.D: Encourage the client to manage the crisis independently before assessing available supports or urgent risk.

candidate.rationale: Current SAMHSA 988 guidance describes early crisis support as beginning with safety assessment, followed by listening to understand how the problem is affecting the person, providing judgment-free support, and sharing or connecting the person with helpful resources. The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan likewise places crisis intervention in Psychosocial Integrity and includes assessing potential violence/safety, identifying the client in crisis, using crisis-intervention techniques, and guiding the client to recovery resources. Therefore B is the priority. A delays immediate safety assessment, C moves prematurely to long-term treatment goals, and D withholds needed assessment and support during an active crisis.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Early crisis support prioritizes safety assessment, understanding the immediate problem through supportive listening, and connection to appropriate resources rather than delaying for comprehensive history or long-term treatment planning.
candidate.source_locator: FAQ sections describing what happens during a 988 call/chat/text: counselor asks about safety, listens and works to understand how the problem is affecting the person, provides personal/judgment-free support, and shares resources or community connections as needed.
candidate.source_organization: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)
